sources.title: Henriette Elvang and Yu-tin Huang, Scattering Amplitudes
sources.locator: Full 270-page book-length PDF retrieved and fetch-verified; read §§2.2, 2.3, 2.4, 2.6 and 3.1–3.3, PDF pp. 9–11, 15–18, 27–45. Spinor factorization and little-group conventions; a scalar contact coefficient; reference-spinor polarizations and Schouten identity; two-line shifts, rational tree poles, factorization residues and the separate large-z condition.

contents.argument: Adapts the massless rank-one factorization and little-group rescaling to the workspace's explicitly stated (-+++) and h=-eta convention; brackets and their normalizations are defined locally.
The book sets the null-spinor rank-one convention; the local lemma directly proves the determinant identity, factorization existence and little-group uniqueness.
Uses the two-line shift and factorization context; replaces the source's Cauchy-contour step with a complete partial-fraction proof under the explicit vanishing-at-infinity hypothesis.
Uses the reference-spinor polarization convention and two-dimensional Schouten structure; proves the pure-momentum shift and contracts only under an explicit conservation hypothesis.

The book gives both a scalar four-point contact coefficient in §2.3 and the independent boundary-term qualification in §3.1; the local proof computes the constant-function pole sum and boundary correction exactly.

sources.title: Andrea Marzolla, The four-dimensional on-shell three-point amplitude in spinor-helicity formalism and BCFW recursion relations
sources.locator: Full 45-page lecture-notes PDF retrieved and fetch-verified; read §§2.1, 3, 4.1–4.2 and the general argument in §5, PDF pp. 5–12 and 28–31. Complex null vector-spinor map, massless little-group scaling, analytic continuation, factorization channels and the separate residue-at-infinity condition.

contents.argument: Independent lecture-note treatment of null vectors as rank-one spinor matrices and little-group rescaling; local signs are fixed to the plan's convention.
The lecture notes independently give the Pauli-matrix norm/determinant relation and complex null spinor variables; the complete finite-dimensional uniqueness proof is local.
Independent lecture-note derivation relates the two-line complex deformation to on-shell factorization and explicitly retains the boundary residue unless separately shown to vanish.
Supports the need to retain a possible boundary term; the constant-function counterexample and its value are verified locally.

sources.title: Ruth Britto, Freddy Cachazo, Bo Feng, and Edward Witten, Direct Proof of Tree-Level Recursion Relation in Yang-Mills Theory
sources.locator: Full 11-page paper retrieved; read §§2–3.1, PDF pp. 2–8. Complex two-line spinor shift, generic rational tree poles, factorization residues and recursion, with the large-z proof explicitly restricted to Yang-Mills helicity cases and its stated diagrammatic inputs.

contents.argument: Section 2 uses the null-momentum bispinor factorization and spinor-helicity conventions; the local definition fixes the equivalent adopted h=-eta signs and brackets explicitly.
Section 2 treats a four-dimensional null vector as a rank-one spinor matrix; the determinant, existence and uniqueness argument are proved locally.

Sections 2–3.1 give the planned two-line deformation, rational pole/factorization route and recursion; the paper proves large-z decay only for specified Yang-Mills helicity cases, so the local theorem retains decay as a hypothesis.
Section 3.1 writes the reference-spinor polarization vectors; the local proposition proves the pure-momentum change and makes current conservation an explicit condition.
The paper derives recursion under its large-z behavior condition; the local counterexample independently computes the omitted boundary correction for a constant coefficient.
